name: Sheariah
title: Israelite who divorced his foreign wife
summary: Sheariah was one of the Israelites from the family of Binnui who had taken a foreign wife in the aftermath of the exile. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of those who responded to Ezra's call to separate from their foreign wives to preserve Israel's religious purity after returning from the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Ezra discovers mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had married women from foreign nations, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: The people confess their sin
keyEvents.description: Ezra prayed and confessed the people's sin before God, and a large crowd gathered and wept with him over this breach of the covenant.

keyEvents.title: Decision to divorce foreign wives
keyEvents.description: The people made a covenant to separate from their foreign wives and follow God's law, as Ezra urged them to do.

keyEvents.title: Sheariah mentioned among those who took foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Sheariah is specifically named among the descendants of Binnui as one who had married a foreign woman and committed himself to sending her away.

keyEvents.title: The Implementation of the Divorces
keyEvents.description: Over a period of three months, the leaders examined all cases where Israelites had taken foreign wives and carried out the divorces to restore the purity of the people.
